data.G: Retain the current src/candidate.cu baseline until research candidates pass correctness and measurement. Integrate only measured, valid programs; remeasure the integrated result and independently confirm it, since gains may not be additive.
data.analysis: Choose N=3: the opportunities are complementary—global pass hierarchy and tile sizing, intra-block reduction mechanics with mapping held fixed, and a launch-avoiding atomic finalization path. A fourth tree would largely duplicate those axes; reserve campaign time for integration and confirmation. Evidence: the supplied baseline is correct and measures 47.079 µs on average over three samples. At n=4,194,304, the current 128-element passes reduce 4,194,304→32,768→256→2→1, implying four reduction-kernel launches followed by a device-to-device copy. The shared-memory reduction synchronizes through each tree level; the source's warp-reduction helper is not used by reduce0. These are code observations, not proof of the bottleneck or of any prospective speedup. Consulted the CUDA 12.6.3 Programming Guide §7.21–7.22: warp reduction support and participating-lane mask requirements inform the intra-block experiment (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/12.6.3/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html). All trees must modify only src/candidate.cu, preserve the run signature and default stream, compute from the current input1 for every valid input, handle tails without out-of-bounds access, and keep scratch accesses within the provided buffer. No additional allocations or external optimized reduction libraries. Validate all required sizes before comparing repeated timings on the frozen GH200/CUDA 12.6.3 target.

children.objective: In src/candidate.cu, investigate reducing the large-n reduction hierarchy to a coalesced tiled first pass plus one final device pass. Sweep useful per-CTA work and block sizes while keeping the complete reduction on-device and using only the provided scratch. Preserve tail safety and correctness for all valid inputs, including n=1, 127, 1024, 65536 and the performance size. Do not use external DeviceReduce-style libraries. Report correctness and repeated whole-call timings for each viable configuration.
children.subject: Large-n global reduction hierarchy and tile sizing

children.objective: Isolate the cost of reduce0's intra-block shared-memory tree: compare a warp-level reduction using valid CUDA sync intrinsics and a correct inter-warp combination, optionally against an allowed CUB block primitive. Hold the global input mapping, block geometry and pass structure fixed during comparisons so this tree measures the block-reduction mechanism rather than changing the hierarchy. Ensure all participating lanes use correct masks/synchronization, including tail blocks. Validate every required size and report repeated whole-call timings.
children.subject: Intra-block reduction primitive and synchronization

children.objective: Test a complete large-n path that zeroes out with cudaMemsetAsync on the default stream, then launches one kernel that reduces each CTA's input tile locally and atomically adds exactly one CTA sum to out. Avoid per-element atomics, extra allocations, stale scratch dependencies, and out-of-bounds tail reads. Compare the cost of the entire memset-plus-kernel call path against the supplied baseline, including correctness at every required size; record the result even if atomic contention makes it slower.
children.subject: Single-kernel atomic finalization with explicit output initialization
